name: Young-Jin Beach Geotube detached breakwater
year_built: not stated precisely; 2006 conference/journal papers already report 12 months of post-construction monitoring, implying construction ~2004-2005 [R1][R2]
status: not stated beyond the 12-month (2005-2006-era) monitoring window; no independent post-2006 status found [R1]
cost: not stated in any source found [R1][R6]
designer: Oh, Y.I. (Rural Research Institute, Korea Rural Community & Agriculture Corporation) and Shin, E.C. (Dept. of Civil & Environmental System Engineering, University of Incheon) [R1]
contractor: not stated; only equipment named (cutter-suction dredge, 50 m barge) [R1]
financed_by: not stated explicitly; Korea's Ministry of Marine Affairs & Fisheries (MMAF) is described as responsible for annual shore-protection works on this coast generally, but not confirmed as this project's specific financier [R1]
motivation: severe winter erosion (waves to 4 m) damaging shoreline scenery and public property; existing tetrapod breakwater was expensive and equipment-heavy; geotube sought as cheaper, faster, scenery-preserving, lower-navigation-risk alternative [R1]
outcome: mixed/spatially uneven over 12 months: shoreline extended 2.4-7.6 m seaward overall; BM2 continuously accreted; BM1 accreted 5.3 m in 3 months then was re-eroded by tidal waves the authors attribute to the structure's own effect on local currents; BM3/BM4 similar but smaller re-erosion; seaweed colonized tubes within 1 year (read as ecologically benign); authors caution long-term effectiveness unproven [R1][R2][R3]
